whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: California generally gives you 2 years from the date of injury to file a claim, but that window shrinks to as little as 6 months if a government entity is involved. Waiting too long can cost you your right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Bar Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you can still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault. We can help sort out how fault gets divided.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in standard injury cases. That means your compensation isn't artificially limited by a statutory ceiling.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you actually recover money. That removes the financial barrier to getting legal help after an accident.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after an accident in Lake Elsinore?
items.answer: In most California injury cases you have 2 years from the date of the accident to file a lawsuit. If a government agency was involved, that deadline can shrink to as little as 6 months, so it's best to act quickly.

items.question: Will I still be able to recover money if I was partly at fault?
items.answer: Yes. California uses pure comparative fault, which means your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault but not eliminated entirely. Even if you share some blame, you may still recover damages.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Lake Elsinore?
items.answer: Public crash records show higher collision counts along corridors such as Railroad Canyon Road, Riverside Drive, Lakeshore Drive, and the I-15. These are simply the roads carrying the most reported traffic volume, not a judgment about any location.
